title: India-US Trade Deal Awaits Preferential Tariff Framework, Says Piyush Goyal
excerpt: Commerce Minister says negotiations on the first tranche are closed but India will not finalize until Washington guarantees a tariff edge over Vietnam, Bangladesh, and other competitors.
body:
• India has closed negotiations on the first tranche of the India-US Bilateral Trade Agreement but is waiting for Washington to provide a preferential tariff framework before finalizing, Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said on Friday.
  • India wants tariff rates that are better than or comparable to those applied to competitors including Vietnam, Bangladesh, Thailand, and China before making the deal operational.
  • Under the interim framework agreed in February 2026, the U.S. reduced its reciprocal tariff on Indian goods from 50% to 18% and removed an additional 25% tariff linked to Russian oil purchases.
  • India's merchandise exports have crossed $200 billion for the current fiscal year by August 21, up more than 15%, with the government targeting $1 trillion in combined goods and services exports.

India and the United States have completed negotiations on the first tranche of their bilateral trade agreement, but the deal remains on hold as New Delhi waits for Washington to establish a tariff framework that gives Indian exporters a clear advantage over competing economies, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said on Friday.

"We have closed the negotiations on the India-US free trade agreement," Goyal said on the sidelines of the India-Belgium High-Level Dialogue on the India-EU Free Trade Agreement in Mumbai, according to ANI. "Given the uncertainties on tariffs in the United States, we are waiting for the US to provide the necessary framework under which India will get a preferential tariff for our exports."

The Tariff Edge India Is Seeking

Goyal has consistently maintained that India will not sign the deal until Washington offers tariff treatment that is equal to or better than what competitors receive. He specifically named Vietnam, Bangladesh, Thailand, the Philippines, China, Malaysia, and Sri Lanka as the benchmarks India is measuring against.

"As soon as the US is able to give us the preferential rate in comparison to our competition, we will finalise the BTA and announce the final details."

— Piyush Goyal, Commerce and Industry Minister

"We have to see the rate that Vietnam pays in another country and what Bangladesh goods are charged. Our rates will be better," Goyal said at a separate national workshop on leveraging free trade agreements.

Where the Interim Deal Stands

The framework for the India-US Bilateral Trade Agreement was announced in February 2026 following discussions between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and President Donald Trump. Under the arrangement, the U.S. reduced its reciprocal tariff on Indian goods from a peak of 50% to 18% and removed an additional 25% tariff that had been linked to India's purchases of Russian oil, after India committed to stopping those purchases.

In return, India agreed to eliminate or reduce tariffs on U.S. industrial goods and a broad range of American agricultural and food products, including dried distillers' grains, tree nuts, fresh and processed fruit, soybean oil, wine, and spirits. India also committed to purchasing more than $500 billion of U.S. energy, ICT, coal, and other products.

However, the tariff landscape has shifted since then. The U.S. imposed an additional 10% tariff on several countries, including India, from July 24 after the U.S. Supreme Court struck down the Trump administration's reciprocal duties as unconstitutional.

India's Broader Trade Push

Goyal said India had secured favorable outcomes in all nine free trade agreements finalized to date, including those with the UK, New Zealand, and the European Union. The India-UK FTA went live on July 15, while the India-EU agreement is expected to come into force in the first quarter of 2027.

He described the EU deal as "game-changing," opening access to a 27-country market with a combined GDP of nearly $20 trillion.

On the export front, India's merchandise exports crossed $200 billion by August 21, up more than 15% year-on-year, with petroleum products, electronics, and engineering goods driving growth. The government is targeting $1 trillion in combined goods and services exports this fiscal year, up from $863 billion last year.

Stakes for Indian Exporters

For India's textile, gems and jewellery, leather, marine products, and MSME sectors, securing a preferential tariff in the U.S. market is critical as they compete against established manufacturing hubs across Southeast Asia.

Goyal also pointed to India's 7.8% GDP growth in the June quarter and said the country is on track to become "an international player of significance" as it works toward its ambition of a $30 trillion economy by 2047. The trade deal with the United States, India's largest trading partner, remains a central piece of that strategy.
